summary_en: MAOUD provides synchronized optical RGB images, multibeam-sonar images and videos, laser point clouds, annotations, sensor extrinsics, and reconstruction-ready sequences acquired with an integrated image-laser-sonar platform. The dataset directly supports acoustic-optical enhancement, detection, and underwater 3D reconstruction research.

title: Three-dimensional aperture-driven photoacoustic tomography (3D-ADPAT)
authors: Xuanhao Wang; Yang Xiao; Yuqi Wang; Xiali Gao; Yongdu Ruan; Xiaohui Yang; Yiyin Su; Dikui Zhou; Xiangdi Li; Yuqian Meng; Zhibo Xiao; Fan Meng; Ruofan Wang; Junhui Shi

summary_en: 3D-ADPAT combines a high-numerical-aperture focused ultrasonic detector with phase-inverted focusing-equivalent reconstruction to address the aperture-sensitivity trade-off in photoacoustic computed tomography. The paper reports improved resolution and contrast and demonstrates whole-body and dynamic volumetric imaging.

summary_en: The 3D-PAULM platform integrates three-dimensional photoacoustic tomography with ultrasound localization microscopy and an NIR-II photoacoustic dye. It enables noninvasive intact-skull whole-brain imaging, combining super-resolution vascular mapping with sensitive tracing of glymphatic transport.

title: All-fiber photoacoustic endomicroscopy reveals layer-specific angiogenesis-oxygenation uncoupling in experimental colitis
authors: Jinying Li; Junye Bi; Di Zhang; Sheng Zeng; Fuwuxing Liu; Peixuan Zou; Ying Shi; Pengqing Sun; Ziyi Ji; Hongxue Jiang; Jian Hong; Long Jin; Yizhi Liang; Wei Huang; Bai-Ou Guan

summary_en: An all-fiber photoacoustic endomicroscopy platform combines high-density fiber-bundle scanning with broadband fiber-optic ultrasound detection for fast dual-wavelength volumetric oxygenation mapping. The system achieves micrometer-scale resolution and reveals layer-specific vascular and metabolic changes in experimental colitis.
